description: SECURITY (s440). The original accept-every-password shape (`hashes.some(h => verifyPassword(pw, h))`, §34 E-ASYNC-STDLIB-IN-SYNC-CALLBACK) wrapped one level deeper: a helper declared INSIDE the server function calls `verifyPassword`, and the helper is used in a `.sort` comparator (no async combinator — DD FORK 2). Before s440 the nested helper escaped every async-colored set, so the comparator received an always-truthy Promise and the build was silent. It now fails closed with the async-stdlib code (the helper's asyncness is rooted in a stdlib call, not a peer server fn).
rationale: §13.2 compiler-managed asynchrony: a Promise-returning stdlib call is auto-awaited where `await` is legal. `matches` wraps one, so `matches` is async; its call in a synchronous `.sort` comparator is an async call the compiler cannot await. §34 E-ASYNC-STDLIB-IN-SYNC-CALLBACK is fail-closed for exactly this position — the nested helper does not launder the Promise.
